threads.body: [Testing] This exercises only the implicit `18098` path, while the newly promised non-default-port behavior is not covered. Add a latest-deps stable-semconv case using a URI such as `couchbase2://<seed>:18099` and assert that `SERVER_PORT` is `18099`; otherwise a regression that drops all Protostellar ports would still pass.

Addressed in f56c0f37c10298fe8ff84fd05e19327359cc4725.

Analysis: The existing test covered only a connection string without an explicit port. Parameterizing it with `:18099` proves that target parsing and span capture preserve a non-default Protostellar port while retaining default-port omission coverage.

Upsides: The test now catches regressions that discard explicit Protostellar ports and also verifies the port-bearing stable span name.

Downsides: The latest-dependency test runs one additional parameterized invocation.

threads.body: [General] This advice targets `ProtostellarBaseRequest`, but Couchbase does not construct that wrapper during normal request-span creation or call `RequestSpan.requestContext` from the Protostellar flow. `ProtostellarRequest` retains and ends the span directly; the wrapper is only created for retry/orphan-reporting paths. As a result, successful `couchbase2://` requests never reach the new `REQUEST_TARGETS` lookup—the test passes only because it manually calls `requestSpan.requestContext(...)`. Instrument the normal Protostellar request/span creation path and apply the core target before the span ends.

Both new matchers require later `ConnectionString`/`CoreProtostellar` signatures, so no advice matches in 3.4.3 even though Muzzle can pass because the referenced classes exist. Add handling for the original signatures or raise the lower bound to the first compatible release.

threads.body: [General] The legacy 3.4.3 path still drops an explicitly configured Protostellar port. `registerFromSeedNodes` only reads `kvPort()` and `clusterManagerPort()`, so the `withProtostellarPort(18099)` used by `CouchbaseProtostellar343Test` is stored as a target with no port; this guard also preserves the already-registered portless target. Consequently those requests emit `server.address=node` but omit the promised non-default `server.port=18099` (the version-specific test currently asserts only the address). Derive the legacy target from each seed's Protostellar port and assert `SERVER_PORT` in the 3.4.3 agent test.

[General] This helper is invoked for every ordinary `Core(CoreEnvironment, ..., Set)` on 3.4.3+, not only Protostellar cores. When a normal Couchbase seed has only a KV/manager port, this code still builds a Protostellar-default target and unconditionally replaces the regular target used by `CouchbaseConfiguredTarget`, so normal spans can lose their configured `server.port` (or get the wrong default semantics). Only replace the core target when the seed set actually contains a Protostellar port; connection-string-derived implicit-default targets are already preserved by the seed-node registration path.

threads.body: [General] This matcher also matches `Core(CoreEnvironment, ..., ConnectionString)`, which is already targeted by `CouchbaseCoreInstrumentation`, but the advice binds `@Advice.This` as `CoreProtostellar`. Since the type matcher covers both classes, applying this advice to `Core` has an incompatible receiver type and can make transformation of ordinary Couchbase `Core` fail. Restrict this constructor matcher to methods declared by `CoreProtostellar`.
